questions.questionText:
The introduction of robots has meant that many firms now require fewer workers to produce their
goods and services.
According to this statement, which factor of production is replacing workers?

options.text: capital
enterprise
labour
land

questions.questionText:
Economics textbooks identify the existence of scarcity as the basic economic problem.
What is it that makes scarcity a problem?

options.text: It can cause inflation and unemployment.
It is impossible to satisfy unlimited wants.
It is the first priority of governments.
It only affects the richest countries.

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a country’s original production possibility curve XX.
manufactured
goods
O X Y
agricultural
goods
What could cause the country’s production possibility curve to move from XX to XY?

options.text: a decrease in the price of manufactured goods
a major war
an improvement in fertilisers
an increase in the employment rate

questions.questionText: What is a benefit of the free market system?

options.text: Innovation is encouraged to increase profits.
Subsidies can be used to encourage exports.
Negative externalities can be controlled.
The distribution of goods and services is fair.

questions.questionText:
A private firm is one of a few suppliers of electricity in an economy. It is fined by the government
for pollution from its coal-fired power stations which affect the health of those living nearby.
What does this situation involve?

options.text: a government policy of nationalising an electricity supplier
a market structure for electricity that is perfect competition
a monopoly electricity supplier that ignores government controls
external costs that are the result of electricity production

questions.questionText: What is not a function of a central bank?

options.text: It is the lender of last resort to financial institutions.
It is the sole issuer of notes and coins.
It lends to individual firms and consumers.
It manages the national debt for the government.

questions.questionText:
Which change will make a manufacturing company replace labour with capital to maintain the
most efficient combination of factors of production?

options.text: The price of machinery has increased.
The productivity of labour has increased.
The productivity of machinery has increased.
The supply of labour has increased.

questions.questionText:
What is the most likely reason a firm might welcome the introduction of a trade union for its
workers?

options.text: Unions advise on the level of company dividends.
Unions press for higher minimum wage rates.
Unions simplify the process of wage bargaining.
Unions wish to operate labour-intensive production methods.

questions.questionText: What is least likely to lead to an increase in consumer spending on a new car?

options.text: a decrease in the cost of car repairs
a decrease in the price of petrol
a decrease in the rate of interest
a decrease in train fares

questions.questionText: What is a characteristic of perfect competition?

options.text: Firms sell an identical product.
New firms cannot enter the market.
The market is controlled by one firm.
There is a high degree of market concentration.

questions.questionText:
A television manufacturer claims to have the most technically advanced production in the
industry.
What is this most likely to mean when compared with its rival producers?

options.text: It has a greater share of the television market.
It is a more diversified company.
It is less likely to be disrupted by strike action.
It needs a more highly skilled workforce.

questions.questionText:
A firm that sells its product for $6 a unit has the following total costs.
output (units) 0 10 20 30
total costs ($) 40 100 120 150
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Average cost is lowest when 10 units are produced.
The firm does not make any profit when 20 units are sold.
The firm has no fixed costs.
Total variable costs fall continuously over these outputs.

questions.questionText:
and under 30 18 15 16
Which statement describes the behaviour of the dependency ratio over the period?

options.text: It falls and then rises.
It falls continuously.
It rises and then falls.
It rises continuously.

questions.questionText: Which statement about fixed costs is correct?

options.text: They exist only in the long run.
They include raw material and direct labour costs.
They increase at the same rate as output.
They must be paid even if there is no output.

questions.questionText:
In many countries the government provides financial help to firms who wish to produce electricity
using wind turbines.
Which kind of policy measure is this?

options.text: deregulation
maximum price
subsidy
taxation

questions.questionText: What is an aim of government policy?

options.text: income tax
interest rates
stable prices
unemployment

questions.questionText:
A government seeks to redistribute income from the rich to the poor.
Which combination of policy measures is most likely to achieve this aim?
income tax sales tax state benefit

options.text: decrease decrease decrease
decrease increase increase
increase decrease increase
increase increase decrease

questions.questionText:
Which situation involving the building industry is most likely to be investigated by a government
body set up to control restrictive practices?

options.text: a builder purchasing a plot of land for development of housing
groups of suppliers of building materials agreeing to fix prices
several builders bidding for the same contracts
several builders using different sources of supply

questions.questionText: What is a likely consequence of economic growth?

options.text: decreased levels of employment
decreased levels of exports
decreased levels of output
decreased levels of poverty

questions.questionText:
A basket of goods is used to calculate a country’s rate of inflation.
What is included in the basket of goods?

options.text: a representative sample of current household spending
all goods bought in the country
the spending on an unchanging group of necessities
the 50 most popular items of household spending

questions.questionText:
There was a fall in investment spending by businesses in the third quarter of 2015.
What would be the likely result of this?

options.text: an increase in economic growth
an increase in exports
an increase in incomes
an increase in unemployment

questions.questionText:
The table shows units of output, value of output and number of people employed in an industry
over three years.
output output value number employed
(units, millions) ($ millions) (000)
year 1 10 10 5
year 2 21 25 7
year 3 32 40 8
What can be concluded from the table?

options.text: Inflation has increased.
Productivity has increased.
Profit has increased.
Working population has increased.

questions.questionText:
Provision of services in rural districts of developing countries tends to occur later than those in
urban areas.
For which service would this not be correct?

options.text: medical research units
mobile phone networks
modern transport systems
university teaching departments

questions.questionText:
The government of a developing country allows a multinational mining company to mine minerals
in order to improve the standard of living of the local people.
Which action by the multinational company (MNC) will not lead to an improvement in the
standard of living of the local people?

options.text: building roads to assist transport
exporting mineral ore
providing skills training
returning profits overseas

questions.questionText: What would have the most severe restriction on the volume of international trade in steel?

options.text: an embargo
a licence system
a quota
a tariff

questions.questionText:
In 2012 the UK held the Olympic Games, which attracted a large number of visitors from foreign
countries.
Which item of the UK’s current account balance will have benefited directly from this event?

options.text: export trade in goods
export trade in services
import trade in goods
import trade in services

questions.questionText:
The table refers to a country’s balance of payments on current account.
$bn
goods exports 100
goods imports 125
services exports 60
services imports 50
income and transfers balance +10
What can be concluded from the table?

options.text: a current account deficit of $5bn
a current account surplus of $5bn
a goods and services deficit of $35bn
a goods and services surplus of $15bn

The table shows the rice yield in four countries.
rice yield
country

China 53
Bangladesh 20
Thailand 20
What may be concluded from this information?

options.text: Bangladesh and Thailand produce the same amount of rice.
Japan produces more than three times as much rice as Bangladesh.
Japan produces the largest amount of rice per hectare.

Japan produces the largest amount of rice per person employed.
